haiku-low.q1: At container start, before readiness. /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys load (secrets_loaded flag, R1/R2).
haiku-low.q2: It retries failed reads 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. Rollout halts with maxUnavailable 0; old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: A refresh timer runs every 300 seconds with jitter, swapping in a changed version id. On failure it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and readiness is unchanged.
haiku-low.q4: Key values live only in process memory. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs.
haiku-low.q5: Only the security on-call can write prod secrets. orders-api-prod has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. Engineers have no read access to prod values.
haiku-low.q6: Git history is not rewritten, so old values remain there. They become useless because the old provider keys are revoked in Step 12.
haiku-low.q7: The holder swaps in the new value by reference. Each provider call reads the key from the holder when built, and sets the Authorization header per call.
haiku-low.q8: Every pod must report the new version id for all three secrets. Provider dashboards must show zero old-key requests, after a 5-minute refresh and 15 minutes observed at baseline.
haiku-low.q9: Store access (Step 2), issue new provider keys (3), copy keys to store (4-5), switch app to store (6-9), remove keys from config (8), revoke old provider keys (12).
haiku-low.q10: From the dev store, using the developer's own identity via R1. It reads only orders-api/dev/*, and no secret is stored on disk.
haiku-low.q11: It retries the failed reads, then logs an error naming the missing secret (no value) and exits non-zero. The pod never becomes ready.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first (R1) at container start, with retries. Only after loading finishes is secrets_loaded set, and /healthz returns 200 (ready) only then.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 attempt plus 3 retries, 2s apart), then logs an error and exits non-zero, restarting with backoff. It never becomes ready, so with maxUnavailable: 0 the rollout halts and old pods keep serving; no customer impact.
sonnet.q3: A background timer every 300 seconds (with jitter) re-reads the store; if the version id changed, the holder swaps in the new value by one reference assignment (in-flight calls keep the old value). On failure (store error, timeout, invalid value) it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, increments a failure counter, readiness unchanged, and alerts if no success for a set period (e.g. 15 min).
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory (in a holder that records its version id; repr redacted). They must never go to disk, environment variables or logs (version ids may be logged).
sonnet.q5: Read prod: only the orders-api-prod identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*); engineers have no prod read. Write prod: only the security on-call.
sonnet.q6: The old values remain in git history (not rewritten) and in old images. They become harmless because every key is rotated at the provider and the old keys are revoked (Step 12) after confirming all instances use the new ones.
sonnet.q7: The key is read from the holder at call time when each provider call is built (Authorization header set per call), not cached in the client.
sonnet.q8: Step 10: every pod reports the new version id for all three secrets (metric or structured log); provider dashboards show zero requests on old keys; wait at least one refresh cycle (5 min) plus the 10-second payment timeout, then observe 15 minutes with error rates at baseline. Any pod on an old version blocks revocation.
sonnet.q9: Set up store/KMS/IAM access (Step 2), issue new keys at providers (Step 3, rotation), write them to the store (Step 4, dev keys Step 5), merge code that reads from the store (Step 6), validate in dev (7), remove keys from the committed file and add CI gate (Step 8), roll out to prod (9), confirm (10), close rollback (11), revoke old keys (12).
sonnet.q10: From the dev store path orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), loaded via R1 by make run, using the developer's own identity; nothing secret on disk.
sonnet.q11: It retries only the missing secret (1 attempt plus 3 retries, 2s apart). If still missing, it logs an error naming the secret and error class (no value) and exits non-zero; it does not become ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Whether and how often to rotate on a schedule is an open question (Q1), undecided; the design would support any cadence.
